findings: Source is Vistry Group PLC Annual Report and Accounts 2025 (Companies House filing dated 13/06/2026 on cover; user treats as FY2025 annual accounts filed 25 Jun 2026). Fiscal period is year ended 31 December 2025 (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzUyNzg4NzYyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Extract ends at page 10 (Chief Executive's review); financial review (p24), cash flow statement (p150), going concern/viability (p83), and independent auditors' report (p134) are referenced in contents but not present in this body text.

FY2025 adjusted revenue £4,155.3m vs FY2024 £4,329.2m (−4.0%); reported revenue £3,613.7m vs £3,779.3m (−4.4%) per 2025 highlights (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzUyNzg4NzYyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

CEO review rounds adjusted revenue to £4.2bn (2024: £4.3bn) on 15,658 completions (2024: 17,225); group average selling price £282k (+3%), reflecting geographic mix and larger open-market homes (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzUyNzg4NzYyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Adjusted operating profit £353.8m (2024: £358.2m); reported operating profit £222.6m (2024: £167.0m) (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzUyNzg4NzYyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Adjusted profit before tax £268.8m (2024: £263.5m); reported PBT £196.2m (2024: £104.9m) (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzUyNzg4NzYyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Adjusted basic EPS 59.3p (2024: 55.9p); reported basic EPS 42.2p (2024: 22.0p); ROCE 13.9% (2024: 14.6%) (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzUyNzg4NzYyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Partner Funded completions 11,593 (−8% vs 12,633) at ASP £246k (2024: £236k), representing 74% of total completions; Open Market 4,065 (−11% vs 4,592) at ASP £391k (2024: £385k), 26% of completions (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzUyNzg4NzYyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Tenure mix within completions: PRS 18% of total (2024: 21%); £106 affordable 26% (2024: 27%); additional affordable 30% (2024: 25%) (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzUyNzg4NzYyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Owned and controlled land bank 71,501 plots (2024: 74,020); strategic land bank 76,368 plots at 31 Dec 2025 (2024: 76,219); 12,599 plots secured across 44 sites in 2025 (2024: 16,508) (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzUyNzg4NzYyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Net debt £144.2m at 31 December 2025 (2024: £180.7m), a £36.5m reduction; average daily debt £734m (2024: £698m). Chair expects to end 2026 with a net cash position and much reduced average daily debt in H2 (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzUyNzg4NzYyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Capital allocation: ongoing share buyback with £29m remaining expected to conclude in 2026; Board to review subsequent distributions thereafter. No dividend per share disclosed in available pages (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzUyNzg4NzYyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

No Building Safety Act, fire-safety remediation provisions, banking covenant headroom, going-concern assessment text, or audit opinion wording appears in the extracted source; only table-of-contents references.

findings: Only interim filing body available: unaudited parent-company interim accounts for the six months ended 30 June 2024, prepared under s836/s838 Companies Act 2006 to confirm distributable reserves for a proposed distribution; approved by the board on 4 September 2024 and stamped at Companies House 06/09/2024 (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzQzNTM3MzAyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Stale versus a 2026 trade view: parent-only, distributable-reserves filing with no consolidated group P&L, cash flow, completions, forward sales, partnership mix, or management guidance; do not treat as a substitute for later group interims (none present in this source).

Income statement compares H1 2024 to the full year ended 31 December 2023, not prior-year H1; H1 2024 profit for the period was £237.8m (dividend income £250.0m, finance income £6.3m, finance costs £18.5m) versus full-year 2023 profit £172.1m (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzQzNTM3MzAyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Note 2 states H1 2024 distributable profits arose from receipt of a £250m cash-settled dividend plus finance income on amounts owed from subsidiaries, offset by external finance costs of £18.5m on borrowing facilities (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzQzNTM3MzAyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Parent cash rose to £151.9m at 30 June 2024 from £18.9m at 31 December 2023; borrowings were broadly flat at £496.5m versus £495.8m, implying parent net debt (borrowings less cash) of c.£344.6m at 30 June 2024 versus c.£476.9m at year-end 2023 (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzQzNTM3MzAyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

Capital return: £100m ordinary share buyback announced 14 March 2024 (commencing April 2024); full £100m treated as reduction in distributable reserves at balance sheet date; 4.0m shares repurchased for £50.5m by 30 June 2024; profits available for distribution £394.8m after own shares held in trust of £9.9m (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzQzNTM3MzAyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

No interim dividend paid in H1 2024 is disclosed; equity statement shows £110.4m dividends paid in full-year 2023 (/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/ch_00306718_MzQzNTM3MzAyMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt).

findings: Vistry Group PLC acquired the 139-hectare former Rugeley Power Station site in Staffordshire from ENGIE; the release does not describe a joint venture or third-party development partner for this deal (source: /workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/0dd1d1a3748702d6.txt).

The brownfield site has undergone extensive remediation and holds outline planning permission for 2,300 homes (source: /workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/0dd1d1a3748702d6.txt).

The planned neighbourhood will include an all-through school, riverside park, commercial space, and homes across affordable, PRS, and open market sale tenures (source: /workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/0dd1d1a3748702d6.txt).

CEO Greg Fitzgerald frames the deal as regenerating a large brownfield site into thousands of high-quality, mixed-tenure homes using placemaking skills; no delivery phasing, start-on-site date, or completion timeline is given (source: /workspace/docs/data/reresearch_director_worker/VTY.L/20260813T120331Z/sources/filings/bodies/0dd1d1a3748702d6.txt).
